summary: Stewart McFarlane worked in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Lancaster University, attested in 1991 and in 2001 within the Department of Religious Studies.

Sthaneshwar Timalsina studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1987–1995) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~2003–2005). Specializing in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, he held posts at Nepal Sanskrit University (~1994–2003), San Diego State University (~2005–2018), and Stony Brook University (~2018).

Stig Wikander studied at Uppsala, Copenhagen, Paris, and Berlin under Arthur Christensen, Henrik Samuel Nyberg, and Geo Widengren. In Indology, Iranian/Central Asian, and religious studies, he served as docent at Lund (1941–1953) and held a chair at Uppsala (1953–1974).

Stuart H. Blackburn studied at Wesleyan University (~1966–1970) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1975–1980). A specialist in Indology and related fields, he held a post at SOAS University of London from circa 1995 to 2011.

Stuart Piggott studied at Churcher's College and under Mortimer Wheeler at University College London and the UCL Institute of Archaeology (~1934–1936). Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, he held a post at the University of Edinburgh from circa 1946 to 1977.
Stuart Ray Sarbacker specializes in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison by 2001 under the doctoral supervision of David M. Knipe.

Su Bai studied at Peking University (1940–1944) under Chengjun Feng, Zuoyun Sun, Rong Geng, and Yongtong Tang. A scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology, he served as professor at Peking University from 1948 until 2004.

Subhadradis Diskul studied at Chulalongkorn, the École du Louvre under Philippe Stern, UCL, and the University of London. In archaeology, he worked at the Bangkok National Museum (~1953–1964) and served as professor, dean, and rector at Silpakorn University between 1964 and 1986.

Subhash Kak studied at NIT Srinagar and IIT Delhi under Pavaguda V. Indiresan. Working in Indology and other fields, he held positions including Delaune Distinguished Professor at Louisiana State University (from 1979) and Regents Professor at Oklahoma State University (from 2007).

Subrata K. Mitra studied at Utkal University, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Rochester. He held posts at the University of Hull (~1982–1989), University of Nottingham (~1989–1994), Heidelberg University (~1994–2014), and National University of Singapore (2015–2018).

Sucheng Chan studied at Swarthmore College (~1959–1963), the University of Hawaiʻi (~1963–1965), and the University of California, Berkeley (~1969–1973). Specializing in history and archaeology, she served as an emerita professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1984).

Sudhakara Dvivedi, an Indologist, studied under Devakrishna. He succeeded Bapudeva Sastri in 1889 and served at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (and Sanskrit College and University) as librarian (1883) and professor of mathematics and astrology (1890, 1898–1905) until circa 1910.

Sudhir Kakar studied at Gujarat, Mannheim, Vienna, and the Sigmund-Freud-Institut. Working in religious studies and Indology, he held posts at IIM Ahmedabad (~1972–1977) and IIT Delhi (1976–1977), as well as visiting appointments at institutions including Chicago, Harvard, and INSEAD.

Sue Hamilton, working in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, completed her D.Phil at the University of Oxford under doctoral supervisor Richard Gombrich and teacher Alexis Sanderson. She held a post at King's College London, attested from 2001 to 2003.

Suehiro Tanemura studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1953 to 1957. He held academic posts at Tokyo Metropolitan University from circa 1968 to 1971 and at Kokugakuin University from circa 1986 to 1998.

Suk Fun Ng completed a PhD in Buddhist studies at The University of Hong Kong (attested 2014), where she studied under doctoral supervisors Jing Yin and Y. Karunadasa and was taught by K. L. Dhammajoti.

Sukhlal Sanghvi studied at Shri Yashovijaya Jain Sanskrit Pathshala and under Balakrishna Mishra. Working in Indology and philosophy, he was professor of Indian philosophy at Gujarat Vidyapith (1922), held the Chair of Jain Philosophy at Banaras Hindu University (1934–1944), and joined Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan (1944).

Sukumar Sen studied at Burdwan Raj College, Sanskrit College, and Calcutta under Suniti Kumar Chatterji and Irach Jehangir Sorabji Taraporewala. In linguistics and Indology, he served at Calcutta as lecturer (1930) and Khaira Professor (succeeding Chatterji in 1954).

Sukumari Bhattacharji studied at the University of Calcutta (~1938–1944) and Jadavpur University (~1960–1964). Active in Indology and religious studies, she taught English at Lady Brabourne College (1945) and was on the faculty at Jadavpur University from 1957 to 1986.

Sulak Sivaraksa studied at Assumption College and the University of Wales, Lampeter (~1954–1957). Active in Buddhist studies and history, he edited for the Siam Society (~1984–1993) and held visiting positions at Cornell (~1976–1977), Berkeley, Harvard, Toronto, and Lampeter.
